claims.statement: Poland permits several deposit-system operators, and official guidance states that each operator may design detailed operations and settlement methods with participating retailers through contracts.
The Polish Ministry states that producers finance collection, transport, recordkeeping, and deposit settlement, confirming that money and records move across the system.
By mid-2026 the Ministry reported billions of returned containers and thousands of reverse-vending locations, indicating live transaction volume rather than a future-only regime.

contrary_evidence: Operators are responsible for settlement design and may provide adequate retailer portals themselves.
The official system has scaled rapidly, which may mean core reconciliation infrastructure is already contracted and difficult to displace.

economics.acquisition_route: Reconcile a historical month for one retail group, prove variances and labour savings, then distribute through POS and accounting partners
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A plausible 5-6 year path would require about 1,500-2,500 stores at roughly 250 PLN average monthly revenue plus event fees, channel-efficient acquisition, and strong retention while founder equity remains high
economics.founder_time: Approximately 12-16 hours per week during the first integrations, with retailer onboarding delegated after templates stabilise
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software subscription and event processing less POS, RVM, operator integration, and support costs
economics.payback: A multi-store group may recover the fee through finance labour and corrected operator statements; the variance pool must be measured from real exports
economics.pricing: About 199-399 PLN per store per month plus 0.005-0.02 PLN per matched return above an included allowance
economics.retention_or_repeat: Deposits and reimbursements recur daily and operator rules remain embedded in monthly close

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A multi-operator mapping of identifiers, statement formats, variance causes, and resolution outcomes could lower integration cost and improve expected-cash forecasts
fingerprint.customer: Polish independent grocery chains, franchise groups, wholesalers, and hospitality retailers participating in the deposit-return system
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Sell through retail-accounting firms, POS integrators, franchise associations, and reverse-vending service companies
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: POS, reverse-vending, manual-return, collection, and operator-statement ingestion with variance alerts and audit-ready receipts
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The retail group pays monthly per location and a small usage charge when return events are matched and an operator-ready reconciliation statement is closed
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A store collects and refunds deposits across products associated with different operators and cannot readily explain a reimbursement or handling-fee variance

founder_fit: High-volume event matching and anomaly detection suit the founder's analytical skill set
The product can begin as a bounded reconciliation audit without holding deposits
A B2B integration model avoids personal-brand dependence
risks: Operator or POS formats may change frequently
Retailers may expect POS vendors to include reconciliation at no extra charge
Small per-item economics require highly automated support
Incorrect discrepancy claims could harm operator relationships

structure.commercial_archetype: Per-location compliance reconciliation SaaS for retailers
structure.control_point: The item-level match among deposit-marked barcode, sale, return, collection, operator statement, and store reimbursement
structure.critical_dependency: Retailers and multiple scheme operators must expose usable event and statement exports with stable identifiers

thesis: Independent Polish retail groups dealing with several deposit-return operators could buy a neutral per-store reconciliation layer that matches POS deposits, reverse-vending or manual returns, operator reimbursements, handling fees, and physical collection events. It would issue evidence packets for discrepancies while leaving deposit custody and statutory operator duties untouched.
title: Deposit Split Ledger Poland
uncertainties: Current frequency and monetary size of store-operator variances
Export and API availability from each operator and reverse-vending system
Which party owns reconciliation under typical retailer contracts
Whether retailer groups prefer a neutral layer to direct bilateral tooling
